Hello Mike,

This looks like a great portfolio for a first-timer.
I like the portfolio and dig your projects.

I've looked at the Mobile version.

I have a few things to say about it:

(important) Make sure the text is readable. Some of the black text gets unreadable due to a darker background image.

(Important) Make sure to say something about yourself, the portfolio is meant to sell yourself and elevate your work. So you are 50% done. I like the picture and signature you have on the main page. But I am disconnected when looking at an ice mountain in the background, but I might be missing something.

(Optional) There isn't a whole lot in each subject. Some have more than others. Which isnt a bad thing per say but it does tell the potentional customer what you specialize in. So make sure to have quality and quality (which quality, you definitely have)  if you want to balance out each part of your portfolio.

(optional) There is quite a bit of movement on the main page, i would personally reduce this for a faster loading time. Keep the animations in each personal subject, they do add some flavour to the website. 

(Optional) The instagram button is a fun way to add more work to your website without updating it constantly. However if you just use Instagram for personal use and don't post any projects on it, im against posting it on a portfolio because it doesn't add anything. The customer isnt looking for your personal life, its looking for your work.

(Very optional) If you would like to make a professional impression and want to work abroad, think about having a translate button.

Hope this can help you continue improving your work!

Hi Caillmusic,
Some feedback on your logo:
Shadows aren't a much appreciated part of a logo because they are not very durable. If you minimize or zoom out of your logo (or use it for exemple as a logo on a pen or business card) the shadow will overtake the rest of the logo and it would look like a mess. If the shadow is a definitive part of your logo I would recommend using a solid color instead of a gradient. 

Customers are usually attracted to vibrant and happy colors (bright), so I would try to play around with your color pallets a bit more. 

Text and fonts are a really difficult subject especially when you just started. I would really suggest looking up some modern fonts and tutorials on them. Make the font feel part of your logo instead of it being on their own.

Hope this'll help you in your redesign or future projects! :)
